editorial:
Ten years after the economy crashed, Australia is a dusty wasteland where people will kill you for a tank of gas. Eric is a quiet, dangerous drifter who loses the only thing he owns—his car—to a gang of thieves. When he finds Rey, the wounded brother of one of the thieves, left behind and bleeding, the two form a tense partnership to track the gang down. The vibe is bleak, slow, and intense, with long stretches of silence that make every gunshot feel louder. Guy Pearce plays Eric like a man with nothing left to lose, and Robert Pattinson surprises as the nervous, damaged Rey.

The movie moves at a deliberate pace, so if you want nonstop action, this might test your patience. But the acting is fantastic, the dusty landscapes look gorgeous, and the tension never really lets up. It's a dark, gritty crime drama that rewards patient viewers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Eric finally catches up to the gang and gets his car back. When he opens the trunk, you learn the real reason he wanted it so badly: his dead dog is inside. He had been trying to bury his only companion. Rey, who had grown close to Eric, is shot and killed during the confrontation. Eric buries his dog, gets back in the car, and drives off alone into the wasteland, leaving everything behind.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark crime dramas and patient, character-driven stories.
